explanation: Helicopter / low-flying aircraft (e.g., covert or unreported military or civilian helicopter)

explanation: Orford Ness lighthouse beam (McGaha); meteor/fireball (24-25 Dec 1980 bright fireball/re-entry); misperception by tired patrolmen
supporting_evidence: Lighthouse in line of sight; fireball documented on 25/26 Dec per some sources

explanation: Lighthouse beam / searchlights; stars; hearsay amplification; later embellishment of Halt statements
supporting_evidence: No contemporaneous documentation of WSA beams; Halt not present
contradicting_evidence: Multiple radio reports claimed; Halt 1991+ statements

explanation: Vehicle malfunction of 15 Sep 1964 LORV-3 test (partial failure; RSO manual cutoff after SECO) causing short fall of RV / anomalous trajectory
supporting_evidence: Launch list records partial failure and manual cutoff on 15 Sep
contradicting_evidence: Cutoff after SECO affects vernier/sustainer phase; RV tumbling & optical flashes not explained; primary launch report not examined

explanation: Commercial power failure/transient at Winifred substation propagating to Echo Flight (Skeptoid; wing history)
supporting_evidence: Wing history logs power fluctuation at E-1 at 1453, transformer short; Alpha Flight precedent 19 Dec 1966
contradicting_evidence: Power failure logged at 1453/1510, ~6 hours AFTER 0845 shutdown; engineering team found no power cause for 0845; unresolved

explanation: Aircraft lights/helicopters, security-flight overflights, stars/planets, light projected on ground, ground vehicle headlights; heightened expectations of frightened guards; Site 9 context of three Atlas fuel explosions (per Cox) raising stress
supporting_evidence: Nevins: only a light; Renninger: helicopters-like lights; launch commanders told guards "military aircraft"; Krause letter notes KC-135
contradicting_evidence: Nevins: night crystal clear with no clouds; Goss: abrupt direction changes; Caplan: ground light not projected from sky (his view)

explanation: Anomalous propagation, ground clutter, birds/insects, wind-farm-like returns (n/a 1960s), tracking noise or false targets; ADC told controllers they were false targets (Selley)
supporting_evidence: ADC reportedly dismissed as false targets; speeds derived from short scope tracks (20 s) are imprecise
contradicting_evidence: Multiple controllers over several years; ADC controller said "Yeah, I see it"

explanation: Electrical/EMI noise or maintenance fault causing spurious indications; false alarms from security system; storm/power anomaly; later conflation of memory (Schuur admits fog)
supporting_evidence: Spurious indicators are known fault pattern (cf. 1966-67 Echo/Alpha events in wing history); Schuur says "I honestly don't know"
contradicting_evidence: Described object-following timeline via PAS; "never" saw a Launch in Progress before/after

explanation: Misidentification of Sirius, Vega, and the B-52 itself (Base Ops dispatcher log: lights correlate with B-52 VOR penetration, low approach, missed approach); anomalous propagation/ball-lightning-like plasma (Blue Book); radar scope artefacts
supporting_evidence: Quintanilla statement; dispatcher log correlation noted in Tulien report (SRC017)
contradicting_evidence: Radarscope film 14 frames; several independent ground observers; B-52 radar paced object 20 mi; pilots saw object near ground

explanation: Unrelated physical intrusion at Oscar-7 LF (padlock open, combination dial moved) at 0449 CDT — possible human intruder activity; distractor or cause of alarm
supporting_evidence: Blue Book/SAC documents (Tulien)
contradicting_evidence: Quintanilla: "does not seem to be related to UFOs"; no tracks found

explanation: B-52 itself (upper airwork, VOR penetration, low approach with landing lights, missed approach) plus haze/inversion explaining many ground sightings (Blue Book discussion)
supporting_evidence: SRC025 text; SRC026 jet-noise entries 0828-0830Z; B-52 on 50-nm radius clearance maneuvering near the area
contradicting_evidence: Timeline: early log entries precede low approach; entries 0940-1010Z after B-52 landed; ground observers distinguished two objects; aircraft cannot explain radar echo on the B-52 itself

explanation: Radar artefacts/natural: meteor echo, anomalous propagation, multiple-trip returns, lightning, ECM/other B-52 radar interference, balloon, satellite, birds/insects (all tested by Shough)
supporting_evidence: Shough: some can explain individual echoes (e.g., meteor for 771-772) at the cost of coincidence
contradicting_evidence: Shough: none convincing for the whole pattern; UHF loss and 20-mi pacing difficult

explanation: Sirius under temperature inversion/haze with scintillation, autokinesis, passing cloud (Blue Book Atch)
supporting_evidence: SRC025; Sirius up at az 132-162 deg, alt 11-23 deg over the log period (EVD029)
contradicting_evidence: Directions in log entries after 0940Z are W of N-7; objects reported hovering at ~500-1000 ft, 50 ft above ground, moving toward observers

explanation: Terrestrial light or other aircraft/ground source seen at long range, with range and height misjudged at night in haze (Blue Book offered "a light on the ground" as an alternative to Vega)
supporting_evidence: Partin form: orange ball "on the ground or just slightly above"; ~15 mi; farm/town lights exist (Bond: Mohall 4 mi from N-7); Vega too faint at ~1 deg altitude (EVD037)
contradicting_evidence: Aircraft passed ~1 mi south and above it (per form); later accounts describe structure; no ground source identified in the file

explanation: Unauthorised entry by someone holding a padlock key, e.g., a current/former Air Police member (three earlier similar incidents were so traced); not connected to the sightings
supporting_evidence: Werlich 31 Oct memo (doc 12); Quintanilla: not related to UFOs
contradicting_evidence: No suspect identified; no tracks found; timing coincident with sightings (0449 CDT)

explanation: Internal malfunction of the B-52 radar/transmitter or an inversion-induced anomalous return (Quintanilla, 30 Oct)
supporting_evidence: Quintanilla; Goff (TDPA) suggested plasma instead; echoes elongated like a rapidly moving target (Shough)
contradicting_evidence: Werlich: radios worked before and after, not a malfunction; discrete moving echoes across 13 scans; Shough: no conventional explanation fully convincing

explanation: Stars, planets (Jupiter, Capella, Saturn, Vega, Altair), satellites (Echo 2), aircraft and meteors seen through a temperature inversion, with group suggestion/mass reporting once a few airmen reported (Blue Book label "inversion effect"; Printy)
supporting_evidence: Reports of 1-2 s colored flashing, star-like sizes, 148 objects from 143 personnel; Jupiter/Aldebaran/Capella in the east-NE sky at 0317-0340 MDT; no positional data, no photos; Hynek-printed log is on the Blue Book (Eastern) clock; under that clock "overhead" = Deneb, "seven/six in the east" = Pleiades, "70 deg azimuth" = Pleiades/Aldebaran, NE = Capella (EVD061); Echo 2 had three visible passes that night (EVD064) but coincidence with log entries is at chance level (EVD065)
contradicting_evidence: Log describes objects moving, stacking and passing through each other, a "UFO 90 miles east at high speed, landed 10 miles east", nine objects in three groups; time zone unresolved; Blue Book gave no case-by-case identification; instrumented theodolite observation; 3:17 flashing-red-light oval, az 120 deg entry, "stacked vertically ... passed through the other two", only two bright NW stars for "four NW" (EVD062); Echo 2 untested

explanation: Low-flying unscheduled aircraft/helicopters or lights seen against dark sky; atmospheric/visual illusions; ball lightning or thunderstorm-type RF interference; anonymous secondhand report with an astronomical error (moon)
supporting_evidence: "No scheduled aircraft" does not exclude unscheduled/military flights; radio interference like a thunderstorm; moon description wrong (EVD071)
contradicting_evidence: 14 SPs + 2 pilots + 1 supervisor independent reports within 3 min; dogs; tower radar off-line so no check

explanation: Hypnopompic/dream experience after dozing in a tower; electrical storm or generator/transformer fault causing outage and alarm cascade; bright star/planet or aircraft beginning the episode
supporting_evidence: Phillips admits he had just awakened from "deep observation"; alarms reset physically; no other witnesses; lack of any report
contradicting_evidence: Detailed, consistent account; power and alarm failure physically recorded? (no record)

explanation: Winter weather: a low cloud/fog/snow-squall deck with a sharp edge hiding stars overhead; commercial power loss with diesel/battery failure; wind/transformer/generator hum; fear and expectation; memory contamination over 28 years; Mills admits the team agreed on a story
supporting_evidence: Weather in the Dakotas in late Dec/early Jan; Echo 1967 wing history (SRC002) links no power event to the 0845 shutdown itself: its power faults came at 1450-1921, hours later, though E-8 was on diesel and its generator ran intermittently at the time; the same history records an Alpha Flight shutdown in Dec 1966 with adverse weather and commercial power failure after the shutdown; so an electrical cause is unproven (corrected 2026-11-16, see EVD085); Mills said the hum stopped outside the fence; the moon is not mentioned (it was 0-7% on 28-31 Dec, 15-67% on 1-6 Jan: EVD074)
contradicting_evidence: Straight edge with angular corners; simultaneous failure of commercial, diesel and battery power; two other teams report similar; officers pulled/passed over (anecdotal)

explanation: Natural predation and scavenging of carcasses (Rommel, CBI, CSU); decomposition effects (bloat, insect and bird activity); hoaxes/pranks; media-driven mass hysteria; misidentified aircraft/stars/planets (Big Mama = a bright star/planet)
supporting_evidence: Official investigations (Colorado CBI 1975, CSU lab study, Rommel 1980); Wikipedia summaries; sheriff photo files not forensically analyzed
contradicting_evidence: Sheriffs/ranchers report clean cuts, no blood, no tracks; lights near scenes; unresolved by independent labs

explanation: Heat-shimmer mirage/optical illusion or aircraft seen against hangars; faulty memory of an event 26 years earlier; the supposed SR-71 departure crowd leaves no other reports
supporting_evidence: No contemporaneous report or Flash message located; Mills himself suggests a heat-wave effect; thousands of potential witnesses yet none reported
contradicting_evidence: Mills and 3-4 companions agreed it vanished; claims of Flash messages are unverifiable

explanation: Weather balloon/Mylar balloon, reflection, or perspective illusions viewed through a cockpit window; no corroboration by crew
supporting_evidence: Other crew did not see it; no radar track; date unknown
contradicting_evidence: Hale describes sudden climbs and high-speed maneuvers over 2-3 minutes

explanation: Conflation: Salas and Meiwald experienced a separate, minor event (UFO sighting by guards at Oscar, no outage) and Salas later merged it with the documented Echo shutdown; or Echo electrical fault only, no UFO
supporting_evidence: Meiwald letter describes a sighting with no outage; Salas flight claims shifted 3 times; wing history documents one shutdown with no UFO; Sheaffer Mars idea
contradicting_evidence: Salas, affidavit and Hastings assert both; Meiwald letter says Oscar; Echo crew vs Oscar crew contested; no documents either way

explanation: Two separate observations were merged: Meiwald team-at-LF report (UFO seen from patrol; minor security alert) and the Salas gate object; plus missile faults electrical; both recollections 44 years later, with Salas leading the 1996 call
supporting_evidence: Salas 2011 email: the two reports came separately; Meiwald does not remember the gate object; transcripts edited by advocate
contradicting_evidence: Meiwald agrees on Oscar, team scared, missile problems; Salas consistent in core elements

explanation: Electrical/EMI cause only; guard report misperceived (vehicle lights, flares, cloud/low object, or humor/prank) or recollected after the fact and shaped by later discussion; Figel himself did not credit it
supporting_evidence: Figel doubted the guard; no contemporaneous record; wing history documents power fluctuations and a transformer short and says UFO rumors were disproven; detail drift (pre-dawn vs after failure; seconds vs minutes)
contradicting_evidence: Figel repeatedly confirms the guard report and the SAT sightings on tape across 2008-10 and 1996; Barlow/Kaminski hearsay of UFO talk; Gamble said superiors altered UFO wording (Klotz via the book)

explanation: Real satellite-overflight security measures (concealment of operations during Soviet reconnaissance satellite passes) or recall drills; unrelated lights reports from WSA guards (aircraft, stars, planets) not logged
supporting_evidence: Cold-war context: tacit acceptance of satellite overflight (NRO), and the testimony itself says no one mentioned UFOs and DeSisto never saw any
contradicting_evidence: No document found describing such alerts; arming off-duty police is odd

explanation: Flare drop by a nearby army unit (Platov, 2004); bright planets/Moon plus rumor and contagion; aircraft or satellite launch/reentry; later embellishment of a base alert
supporting_evidence: Official Soviet explanation; sky check shows a near-full Moon rising ENE ~2000 MSK and Venus, Jupiter, Saturn and Mars low in the SW-W at dusk (EVD091); base is an SS-20 site per INF MOU (EVD092)
contradicting_evidence: Plantonev saw a disc making a turn without sound; ABC says town-wide reports of a huge hovering saucer for hours; flare burns only 5-7 minutes

explanation: Misidentified ordinary lights plus contagion among a night shift; aircraft/helicopter lights; flares/test; later reinterpretation
supporting_evidence: No astronomical match: Moon below horizon, Venus and Mars set by ~2400, only Saturn S and Jupiter near horizon after 0100 (EVD091); testimony is consistent in the quoted depositions
contradicting_evidence: Seven depositions; low hover 20-70 m; beam; two-hour duration; fighter evaded; KGB file not seen by me

explanation: Classified test activity or helicopters at an alarm-prone test range; bright misidentified lights; later folklore (Bennewitz affair)
supporting_evidence: AFOSI says no aerial tests in Coyote Canyon (only ground tests); Sandia/DOE/AFWL denied responsibility (secondary summary); sky check shows no Moon or bright planet at 2350 (EVD091)
contradicting_evidence: Three SPs and a Sandia guard; radio failure; AFOSI document is real

explanation: Bright planets at dawn (Venus rising in the east ~0500-0530 and Jupiter low in the west in March), autokinesis and stress; helicopters; aircraft
supporting_evidence: Sky check EVD104: Venus (-3.8) rose in the east and Jupiter (-2.3) stood low in the west on plausible dates; Brown himself told the FSC it was probably a helicopter
contradicting_evidence: Two teams 10 mi apart; erratic motion; lasted ~2 h; direction not recorded

explanation: Flock of birds or high aircraft formation glinting in sun; balloons; ice-crystal optics
supporting_evidence: No planet at 75 deg elevation (EVD104); five white objects in formation fit birds or an aircraft formation; towers saw nothing
contradicting_evidence: Hovering twice; triangular shape; two witnesses

explanation: Venus (m-4.5) rising ~0310 in the ENE with Mars nearby, scintillation/colour changes (Ortiz); Jupiter in the SSE evening for the campers; aircraft, meteors
supporting_evidence: Venus rises at ~0310-0330 MDT in the ENE, color-changing and visible for hours, matches a 3-hour object first noticed ~0300 (EVD104)
contradicting_evidence: Ortiz describes a disc with notches; camper description of merging lights does not match Jupiter

explanation: Meteor fireballs (night of 19 Jan 1995) for the green fireball; low aircraft/helicopter lights for the first object
supporting_evidence: Spokesman-Review 21 Jan 1995: Thursday-night green fireball over the Northwest judged a meteor (SRC057); technician put the fireball after midnight vs news ~2000
contradicting_evidence: Slow, low, multi-colored light seen long enough for a radio exchange

explanation: First group (~2000): aircraft in formation (Operation Snowbird A-10s, per Wikipedia); second group (~2200): flares dropped by A-10s on the Goldwater range (Luke AFB, 1997)
supporting_evidence: Air Force statement and later analysis that flare luminosity fits at 50-70 mi (secondary, SRC058)
contradicting_evidence: Many witnesses describe a solid wedge; lights were reportedly in fixed positions

explanation: Moon, Saturn and bright stars rising in the east (EVD104; observation time not given); aircraft; farmers misperceiving distance; predation/scavenging for the cattle
supporting_evidence: On 11 Dec 2006 Saturn rose ENE ~2200 and a 54% Moon rose ~2400 in the east; Capella, Aldebaran, Sirius, Betelgeuse were up
contradicting_evidence: 7 Dec fast 90-degree turn; blue/red/white lights seen with binoculars for 30 min

explanation: Aircraft formation (Ellsworth hosts B-1B bombers) seen below fog/low cloud; reflections
supporting_evidence: No astronomical match (EVD104); witnesses saw a rigid lighted formation hover for seconds
contradicting_evidence: 5-10 s duration; two witnesses; no sound noted

explanation: Project Mogul balloon train (NYU Flight 4) plus later conflation with other events (test dummies, 1956 KC-97 crash, 1959 balloon mishap); no recovery of aliens (USAF 1995 and 1997 reports; AARO Vol. I)
supporting_evidence: USAF 1995/1997 reports and AARO Vol I (primary): materials consistent with Mogul; bodies reports conflated with dummies and later accidents; GAO found no July 1947 air-accident report for the site
contradicting_evidence: Rudiak/Sparks challenge Flight 4 landing; Marcel, Haut, Proctor describe material unlike a balloon; Haut affidavit and Exon/Lytle hearsay

explanation: Memory contamination and later embellishment (Haut late-life dementia per Randle; hearsay chain; 40 years of lore); affidavit prepared by researchers
supporting_evidence: Randle says Haut was confused; Carey and Schmitt wrote the affidavit from "hints"; daughter says he approved it
contradicting_evidence: Notarized and witnessed; Haut wrote the 1947 press release

explanation: Misidentified routine test film (chaff/bloom artifacts) with AARO linking the claimed 1964 reentry-vehicle shoot-down to an anti-ballistic-missile test
supporting_evidence: AARO Vol I: film not recovered; time and place correlated with an ABM test
contradicting_evidence: Jacobs and Mansmann insist on CIA film confiscation

explanation: Misperception of a bolide/fireball seen that evening (green flashes reported on TV; the green/blue fast object elsewhere) with a separate, closer slow object (aircraft, helicopter or lights) at Bangor; observer-position/size-distance error
supporting_evidence: No astronomical object at 2122 PDT could account for a low slow disc in the west (EVD118); the fast green object seen across WA/OR/BC resembles a bolide but the date lacks any fireball record I could find
contradicting_evidence: Swanson saw detail (ring, dark centre) not reported by others; low altitude over the base only; Hastings cannot place other witnesses

explanation: Arcturus low in the west (Junkin, 2100 PDT, 16 Sep 2004: mag -0.05, altitude ~21 deg due west) scintillating through the lower atmosphere, plus a jet or helicopter; other reports are aircraft, helicopters (a Blackhawk is mentioned), flares and fireballs
supporting_evidence: Arcturus was the brightest star in the west at about the stated time and place (EVD118); Junkin considered and rejected a bright star
contradicting_evidence: Two adults and four children saw it; second light flew in and both lights extinguished together

explanation: The setting nearly full Moon (97%, alt ~14 deg SSW) or Mars (m-0.5, alt ~9 deg SE) seen with smoke and glow, or a fire plume/glow, at ~0425 MSD; radiation change due to the observers changing position/shielding
supporting_evidence: Moon and Mars were both low and orange-tinted (EVD118); instruments and positions undocumented
contradicting_evidence: Multiple accounts; Pravda article is a 2002 retrospective

explanation: Bright fireball/meteor (fast, low-looking, yellow-orange, passing overhead), or an aircraft; the zigzags come from a Marine hearing sailors second-hand; observers on a ship at night judge altitude poorly
supporting_evidence: Entry itself says fast, low-altitude; no radar or other corroboration in the log; Handelman suspected an aircraft
contradicting_evidence: Several sailors reportedly saw it and described an oval, silent, orange object; the book reports zigzag motion

explanation: Chance and base rate: with 5-6 test series and ~45 shots, 9-17% of days in 1951-1955 fall within 3-10 days of a shot, and fallout spread across the whole U.S.; meteors (including a very active 1948-51 green-fireball period over NM predating Nevada tests) and observer expectation after publicity
supporting_evidence: Base-rate calculation (EVD124); fireballs reported at Los Alamos and Sandia before 1951 where no fallout existed (Wilson himself notes this)
contradicting_evidence: Wilson claims regional match of fallout trajectories and reports; no systematic data published

explanation: Jupiter (m-2.7) was high in the west at ~0400 local (alt ~60, az ~282) and the brightest steady object up (Marquez); Moon/Mars/Jupiter or stars at the evening time for Kramer; autokinesis and perspective on a ship; no radar contact
supporting_evidence: EVD125: Jupiter fits Marquez (not twinkling), fixed relative bearing on a steady course, though Marquez put it 40-45 deg up
contradicting_evidence: Marquez saw it descend and rise; Kramer saw zigzags; crews found it odd

explanation: Anomalous radar returns (weather or ionized cloud, as the Ivy history says) or the British Canberra at a higher altitude than planned; Hasty may be misremembering altitude
supporting_evidence: DNA 6035F: RAF Canberra samplers at Kwajalein; code name for Canberras is Eager Beaver and VIKING was VIP aircraft (EVD126)
contradicting_evidence: Hasty insists on multiple aircraft targets above 60,000 ft visible to pilots

explanation: Expectation after the Levelland wave of 2-3 Nov 1957, bright full Moon rising in the ENE (alt 19-29), Venus and bright stars low; aircraft; guards at a high-security site primed for intruders
supporting_evidence: EVD127: full Moon rising ENE and Venus setting WSW during the guards half hour
contradicting_evidence: Three objects 50 ft up; patrolman saw a light; reporters saw red and green lights low in the north

explanation: Conflation of the Echo events (16 Mar), the documented Belt sighting (24 Mar) and routine multi-site restart nights; hangar rumor ("UFO") spreading before any official word; memory of dates and missile counts drifting over 37 years; Echo experience of a spring-1967 shutdown transposed to Oscar
supporting_evidence: Salas, Jamison and Klotz disagree on date and number (Klotz asks for documents); Evans recalls nothing for Oscar on 16 Mar; the wing history documents one shutdown; Jamison saw no UFO and was not asked to sign anything
contradicting_evidence: Belt (24 Mar) is documented in Blue Book and the Tribune with Malmstrom helicopter/ground search next morning, consistent with Jamison hearing about it; several witnesses (Koertner, Jamison, Meiwald) recall an Oscar event

explanation: Echo-2 sighting after the 0845 shutdown (camper team incident in the afternoon or evening) is not a cause of the shutdown; ring of lights around a perimeter light in falling snow (halo or lens effect) and later rumor attached to the shutdown
supporting_evidence: Wing history gives the shutdown at 0845 and power events at ~1450; Barlow places the camper incident after his team was recalled and says he was told later at Echo-1
contradicting_evidence: Barlow reports confiscated film and SAC brass at Echo-1
